# Apple | halo_rev_a | halo_replica — every axis, and which is better on it

*L9 — THE COMPARISON, halo Replica, 2026-09-05. **Generated by `tools/k_threeway.py render` from `comparison/threeway.json`. Nothing on this page is hand-typed into it.***

**Anchor check at render time: 80 PASS · 0 FAIL · 0 CANNOT DETERMINE → PASS.** Every cell below names a file and a value in it; `k_threeway check` resolves all of them and goes red when the table and its sources disagree.

---

## What this is

Apple | halo_rev_a | halo_replica, one row per axis. Five lanes measured Apple's board and nobody had set our own two boards against each other. This file is that comparison, and it is the artifact DECISIONS.md D23 asked for: it converts twenty-two assertions into measured differences, or says CANNOT DETERMINE and names what would settle it.

## The asymmetry that governs every row

> THE THREE OBJECTS ARE NOT THE SAME KIND OF THING, and no row means anything until that is stated. Apple's AirTag is a shipped product. halo_rev_a is a routed, DRC-checked, priced KiCad design with 62 footprints, 49 vias and 255 track segments. halo_replica is a MEASURED DRAWING: one face, no copper, no nets, no netlist, no DRC, no price, and no possibility of any of those, because nothing in it was ever a schematic. A Replica row that wins on fidelity has not thereby won anything a person can build.

## The three axes a row can be judged on

- **F** — FIDELITY TO APPLE — does this object reproduce what Apple actually built. The Replica's stated purpose (Leif: 'a perfect copy of the internal airtag stuff').
- **B** — BUILDABILITY — can it be ordered, assembled and checked. Measured against published capability pages and against this repo's own DRC/DFM/cost outputs.
- **G** — FITNESS FOR GOAL.md — a cheap open Find My puck, an embeddable circuit block in any outline, and peer-to-peer ranging between Leif's own sensors.

**Better is not automatic.** D23, verbatim: 'some of Core's divergences will survive comparison — the deleted amplifier looks likely.' It did. So did four more. Every row names the axis it is judged on, and where the axes disagree the row says so instead of picking the flattering one. CLOSER TO APPLE IS NOT A SYNONYM FOR BETTER and is never used as one here.

## The accumulation — the divergence counter

*THE-DRIFT.md's own prescribed fix, verbatim: 'A divergence budget, made visible. That count belongs on the convergence scoreboard as a tracked row with a stated ceiling, so the thirteenth divergence is visibly the thirteenth rather than just the next one. A ratchet with no counter is how you get here.' This is the counter. It is computed from the rows above by tools/k_threeway.py, not typed.*

| | SAME | EQUIVALENT | DIVERGED | MISSING | CANNOT DETERMINE | UNSTARTED | n/a | departures | NO ANSWER |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **halo_rev_a** | 5 | 2 | 12 | 1 | 3 | 0 | 2 | **13** | **3** |
| **halo_replica** | 9 | 0 | 1 | 1 | 8 | 4 | 2 | **2** | **12** |

**THE TWO RIGHT-HAND COLUMNS MUST BE READ TOGETHER AND NEITHER MAY BE QUOTED ALONE.** The Replica's 2 departures against rev_a's 13 looks like a rout and is not one: the Replica also has NO ANSWER on 12 of 24 axes against rev_a's 3. An axis you never answered cannot be a departure. Quoting the departure count on its own would be this project's own headline-from-a-favourable-half failure, in the document written to catch it.

- **SAME** — the same thing, or inside the bound Apple's own value is known to within. No departure.
- **EQUIVALENT** — a different realisation doing the same job to the same specification.
- **DIVERGED** — a deliberate difference from what Apple built. Includes functions DELETED.
- **MISSING** — the function is absent and nothing replaces it.
- **CANNOT DETERMINE** — MEASURED AND NOT SETTLED. An attempt was made, it is on record, and what would settle it is named.
- **UNSTARTED** — NOT ATTEMPTED. Distinct from CANNOT DETERMINE and the distinction is the point of the count below: an unstarted axis is a job, a CANNOT DETERMINE is a limit.

**The ceiling.** THERE IS NO CEILING, because nobody has set one. THE-DRIFT.md asks for 'a stated ceiling' and no document in this repo states a number. That is an open product decision and it is routed to the orchestrator, not decided here.

### What the count says

- halo_rev_a departs from Apple on 13 of the 24 axes (12 DIVERGED + 1 MISSING). D23's own sentence says halo 'had diverged from the AirTag in seven places'. The full three-way count is nearly double that. THE RATCHET WAS WORSE THAN THE DOCUMENT THAT NAMED IT — which is exactly what a ratchet with no counter does.
- halo_replica matches Apple on 9 axes and HAS NO ANSWER ON 12 (8 CANNOT DETERMINE + 4 UNSTARTED). Half the table.
- AND THE NINE MATCHES ARE ALL IN ONE REGION. Outline, shape, thickness, layer count, centre hole, finish, and the three refusals where the right answer was to draw nothing. THE REPLICA MATCHES APPLE ON THE BARE BOARD AND HAS NO ANSWER ON ALMOST ANYTHING MOUNTED TO IT. That is a true and useful object; it is not a replica of the AirTag's internals, which is what was asked for.
- The four UNSTARTED axes are one job, not four: Apple's BACK face has never been drawn. Battery contacts, the five bulk capacitors, the ~38 test points and half the coverage all sit on it, and oflynn-frontside-fullres.jpeg (2347x2344) already carries every one of them. It is the highest-value unblocked work in this lane by a wide margin.

### The GOAL.md re-read

*'Periodically read GOAL.md and ask one question in writing: does what we are building still answer this? Record the answer even when it is yes, because a check that only produces output when something is wrong is a check nobody trusts.' Run here, 2026-09-05, against the accumulation rather than against any single row.*

**GOAL 1 a perfect copy of the AirTag internals** — NEITHER OBJECT ANSWERS THIS, and they fail it in opposite directions. rev_a is a functional equivalent with 13 named departures. The Replica is a faithful substrate with the electronics absent — it matches the board and not the internals, and 'internals' is the word Leif used. ANSWER: NO, for both, for different reasons.

**GOAL 2 an embeddable block not only a puck** — rev_a answers it: a KiCad hierarchical block with the antenna in its own copper, which is exactly why row 6's fidelity loss is a GOAL win. The Replica cannot answer it and cannot be made to — it has no schematic, no netlist and no nets, so there is no block to embed. ANSWER: YES for rev_a, STRUCTURALLY NO for the Replica.

**GOAL 3 local relative position between Leifs own devices** — rev_a answers it with Bluetooth Channel Sounding on the nRF54L10 — the one capability in the whole comparison that Apple does not provide at any price. The Replica does not address it. ANSWER: YES for rev_a, NOT ADDRESSED by the Replica.

**CONSTRAINT cost is a first class spec** — rev_a is priced at 10/100/1000/10000 against a dated catalogue and FAILS honestly at two of them on stock. The Replica has no cost, no sourced part, and a board that is not orderable at either house. ANSWER: YES for rev_a, NO for the Replica.

### The conclusion

THE-DRIFT.md says halo 'built the wrong thing while every step was right'. Measured against GOAL.md rather than against the AirTag, THAT IS TOO HARSH ON rev_a AND TOO KIND TO THE PROCESS. rev_a answers three of GOAL.md's four stated aims and is the only one of the two objects that answers any of them. What actually went wrong is narrower and worse: Leif asked for BOTH — 'so create many different versions including one which is a perfect recreation' — and the project built the equivalent and did not build the recreation until he said so twice. The defect was never that rev_a diverged. It was that the recreation was not also built, and that nothing counted the divergences while it wasn't.

### And the risk in this very document

The failure THE-DRIFT.md describes is a sequence of locally-correct judgements arriving somewhere nobody chose. THIS FILE COULD REPEAT IT by letting 'closer to Apple' accumulate into 'better'. It does not: on the primary axis of each row halo_rev_a wins 12 and halo_replica wins 7. The Replica's wins are real and they are concentrated in one region of the board, and this document says so in the same breath as it counts them.

## Distance from a deliverable — the other axis of drift

*The divergence counter in threeway.json counts distance FROM APPLE. It does not count DISTANCE FROM A DELIVERABLE, and that is the gap that let this project run for a day with 130 measurement files, 40 measuring tools and twelve evidence documents, and NOTHING ANYONE CAN OPEN IN KiCAD OR SEND TO A FABRICATOR. We had an instrument for one axis of drift and none for the other, so the Replica could move steadily away from being a buildable thing while every number about fidelity improved. THIS IS THE MISSING AXIS. It is red until KiCad can open something.*

**5 of 8 artifacts exist and open. 0 of those are STALE. 4 rows are green.**

| | artifact | state | opens | current | source ok | **its own verdict** | evidence |
|---|---|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|---|
| D1 | Schematic source | ✅ | yes | — | — | — | `electronics/halo_replica/out/schematic/halo_replica.kicad_sch` |
| D2 | Netlist | ✅ | yes | yes | — | — | `electronics/halo_replica/out/schematic/halo_replica.net` |
| D3 | Footprint library | ✅ | yes | — | — | — | `electronics/halo_replica/halo_replica.pretty/REPL_0201_0603Metric.kicad_mod`, `electronics/halo_replica/halo_replica.pretty/REPL_0402_1005Metric.kicad_mod`, `electronics/halo_replica/halo_replica.pretty/REPL_ABSENCE_EYEBALLED.kicad_mod`, `electronics/halo_replica/halo_replica.pretty/REPL_BACK_CONTACT_POS.kicad_mod`, `electronics/halo_replica/halo_replica.pretty/REPL_BPAD_D0.21.kicad_mod`, `electronics/halo_replica/halo_replica.pretty/REPL_BPAD_D0.34.kicad_mod` |
| D4 | Board file | 🔴 | no | — | — | — | no file of this kind anywhere in this tree |
| D5 | ERC result | ✅ | yes | yes | — | 0E | `electronics/halo_replica/out/schematic/halo_replica.erc.json` |
| D6 | DRC result | ⚠️ | yes | ? | yes | **33E 0U** | opens, but its source D4 (Board file) does not exist in this tree, so there is nothing to be newer than. UNMEASURED, not stale. |
| D7 | Gerbers | 🔴 | no | — | — | — | no file of this kind anywhere in this tree |
| D8 | Drill file | 🔴 | no | — | — | — | no file of this kind anywhere in this tree |

**Freshness.** AN ARTIFACT THAT OPENS IS NOT AN ARTIFACT THAT IS CURRENT. halo_rev_a's gerbers open perfectly and describe a board that no longer exists: they carry an embedded KiCad creation date of 2026-09-05T06:06:39 while the board file they came from has an mtime of 07:54:19 - 6,460 seconds later, an hour and three quarters in which the board gained the NFC coil keep-out, lost plane copper under the coil, and was rerouted from 83 unconnected items to 28. A pure existence test reads that GREEN. EXISTENCE IS ADJACENT TO CURRENCY, which is the same failure shape as every other control this lane broke today.

**The rule.** Every non-root artifact must be NEWER THAN EVERY ONE OF ITS SOURCES. A set of files is only as fresh as its OLDEST member; a source is as new as its NEWEST member. Both directions are the conservative one. FRESH -> the row can be green. STALE -> RED. SOURCE ABSENT -> CANNOT DETERMINE, never green and never red: an artifact with no source to compare against is UNMEASURED, not stale, and this project does not let an unmeasured thing occupy the same field as a measured one.

**Timestamps.** An EMBEDDED timestamp - one the generating tool wrote into its own output - is preferred wherever it exists. mtime is the fallback and it is WEAK: a git checkout rewrites every mtime to checkout time, which can make a stale artifact look fresh or a fresh one look stale. Every row records which kind it used, and a comparison that mixes an embedded stamp against an mtime says so.

**Its own verdict — the column that removes a trap rather than documenting it.** A REPORT'S ROW STATE AND A REPORT'S CONTENTS ARE DIFFERENT FACTS, and with only three columns the first reads as the second. D6 showed valid=yes, which by this file's own rules means ITS SOURCE (the ERC) was clean - and reads to anyone scanning a table for green as 'the DRC passed'. It did not: the Replica's DRC reports 42 errors against 3 warnings, with actual clearances down to 0.0000 mm. The column that says so is now beside it. Documenting the trap was the weaker option; removing it is this one.

> **A report row being GREEN means:** the report EXISTS, OPENS, is NEWER than the thing it grades, and came from a source that had itself passed. It says NOTHING about what the report FOUND. A DRC listing 42 errors is a perfectly good ARTIFACT and a perfectly bad BOARD - different objects, and this table now shows both.

> **And a failing report does not turn its own row red**, because the artifact is not the defect. Turning D6 red on its contents would conflate 'we have no DRC' with 'the DRC found things', and this project already has a standing rule against conflating could-not-build with could-not-verify. Contents become a GATE where something DEPENDS on them - which is exactly what the third leg does for D7 and D8.

### The fifth state — whose fault a clearance violation is

42 of the Replica's 45 DRC violations are clearance errors on rows placed at MEASURED positions and sizes. An overlap there means one of three things and only one is a defect: Apple's metal genuinely is that close, OR our measurement could not separate two adjacent features, OR we drew something wrong. A gate that cannot tell them apart gets switched off for crying wolf - the same way an mtime-only freshness rule gets switched off the first time it calls a clean clone stale.

**IF A VIOLATION CAN MOVE OUT OF DRAWN-WRONG BY EDITING A STRING, THE GATE BECOMES SOMETHING A LANE IMPROVES BY TYPING. So every excusing class carries a RESOLVABLE POINTER that this check resolves AND CHECKS SUPPORTS THE CLAIM. A pointer that resolves but does not support the claim is refused exactly like one that does not resolve.**

**The default is the honest one.** DRAWN-WRONG needs no pointer and is what an UNCLASSIFIED violation falls back to. Silence means our fault, never Apple's. A lane that wants a violation excused must produce evidence; a lane that produces nothing gets the blame. The incentive runs the correct way round.

| class | pointer required | blocks fabrication | means |
|---|:-:|:-:|---|
| **DRAWN-WRONG** | no | **yes** | we placed something wrong. Our defect, and the default. |
| **MEASUREMENT-LIMITED** | yes | **yes** | the two features are closer together than our measurement could separate, so the overlap is an artifact of resolution rather than a placement error. NOT OUR DEFECT AND STILL NOT FABRICABLE - you cannot cut a board where two pads overlap, whatever the reason. It blocks, and it names a different fix: a measurement that CAN separate them, not a nudged pad. |
| **GENUINELY-TOUCHING** | yes | no | the two features are the same net or the same physical feature, so there is no clearance to violate. The rule fired on a distinction that does not exist on Apple's board. |
| **BOUND-LIMITED** | yes | **yes** | copper-to-OUTLINE, where our outline's diameter is a BOUND (24.95-26.34 mm) and not a number. No placement change fixes these honestly: the violation is against an edge whose position is not known. Specified by the board lane, not invented here. |

**Resolution floor: 0.0606 mm.** TWO genuine pixels at the coarser of this face's two genuine resolutions: 2 / 33 px/mm = 0.0606 mm. One pixel of edge-location uncertainty on each of the two facing edges. *Not the registration hold-out:* The handoff's held-out registration error is 0.1256 mm, and using THAT as the floor would excuse roughly twice as many violations. It is the wrong number here: a global registration error is COMMON-MODE between two features measured in the SAME frame and very largely cancels out of the gap between them. Reaching for the larger number would have been the permissive direction dressed as rigour. *Not one pixel:* one pixel would credit a single edge with perfect location while the other carries all the error. Two edges, one pixel each. *What would sharpen it:* a measured edge-location repeatability on this face - two independent extractors on the same edges, the way the outline lanes measured 0.0158 mm median across 1182 shared rays on the other face. Nobody has done that here, so this floor is derived rather than measured, and it says so.

**Current split of 33 clearance errors in `electronics/halo_replica/pcb/out/halo_replica.drc.json`:** DRAWN-WRONG **33** · MEASUREMENT-LIMITED **0** · GENUINELY-TOUCHING **0** · BOUND-LIMITED **0** — 33 block fabrication. no classification file found - every error falls back to DRAWN-WRONG. That is not CANNOT DETERMINE: an unexcused violation IS our defect until evidence says otherwise.

**The rule.** A ROW IS GREEN ONLY WHEN A FILE EXISTS THAT THE RELEVANT TOOL CAN ACTUALLY OPEN. A path that exists is not an artifact. Every row therefore carries a FORMAT PROBE - a string the real format must contain - and an empty file, a stub, or a file of the wrong kind at the right name all stay RED. The selftest watches each of those three cases fail on purpose, because a check that only ever goes red proves nothing about its own ability to go green.

**Anti-gaming.** The board and schematic rows additionally REFUSE a file whose sha256 matches halo_rev_a's equivalent. The cheapest way to turn this check green without doing the work is to copy the board Leif rejected into the Replica's tree, and that would be the exact failure this check exists to catch, dressed as a pass.

Why each is required, in the row's own words:

- **D1 Schematic source** — There is no circuit until there is a schematic. Every net, every part and every connection the Replica claims to copy from Apple lives here or lives nowhere.
- **D2 Netlist** — The netlist is the schematic in the form the board tool consumes. Without it a board file is a drawing of copper rather than a realisation of a circuit, and nothing can check that the copper matches the schematic.
- **D3 Footprint library** — Apple's parts are WLCSP-50, WLCSP-10, 0201 and a wound coil. None of those has a stock footprint that fits this board, and the Replica's whole claim is that its geometry is measured rather than assumed. The measured geometry has to become land patterns or it is not in the design.
- **D4 Board file** — THIS IS THE ONE LEIF ASKED FOR. His words were 'the exact pcb design and all the components'. Until this row is green there is no PCB design, only an apparatus for measuring one.
- **D5 ERC result** — A schematic nobody ran the rule checker over is a claim, not a verified circuit. This project's own standard is that a check which never ran is verification debt.
- **D6 DRC result** — Same argument one level down, and it is the row THREE-WAY.md row 23 turns on: halo_rev_a is a design that CAN be wrong and is measured to be wrong in four height rows. The Replica cannot be wrong in that sense at all, because there is nothing to check.
- **D7 Gerbers** — A board file is what WE can open. Gerbers are what a FABRICATOR can open. Nothing gets made without them. *halo_rev_a HAS NOT GOT THESE EITHER. This row is red for both boards, and saying so is the point - a check that only accuses the Replica would be measuring the wrong thing.*
- **D8 Drill file** — The board is annular with a routed centre pocket and three plated tooling holes. Every one of those is a drill or route operation and none of them exists until this file does. *halo_rev_a HAS NOT GOT THIS EITHER. Red for both.*

## Reconciliation with the prior comparison

*The brief's instruction: read out/comparison/ and docs/COMPARISON.md and say whether these numbers agree, and where they do not. They mostly agree. Three rows do not, and one of the three matters.*

**Denominators.** docs/COMPARISON.md grades 34 rows (22 component + 12 PCB) and counts 18 DIVERGED + 2 MISSING = 20 departures. This file grades 24 axes and counts 12 DIVERGED + 1 MISSING = 13. THESE ARE NOT THE SAME MEASUREMENT AND 20 vs 13 IS NOT A CHANGE. The prior page grades parts; this page grades axes, and one axis can hold several parts (row 9 holds Apple's flash, its LDO and its load switch, which are three rows there and one here).

### Where they agree

- 6 of 18 Apple BOM lines carry a usable manufacturer part number; 9 of 18 carry none at all. Not re-derived here and not disputed - it is a BOM fact, not a board fact, and it remains the real ceiling on 'recreating it exactly', higher than the U1 wall.
- Board thickness DIVERGED for rev_a, with D17's reason. Agreed, and this file adds that the Replica's faithful 0.30 mm is what makes it unorderable.
- Connectors SAME, battery contacts SAME, populated sides SAME. Agreed on all three.
- The U1 wall. Agreed, and unchanged: neither board has a UWB radio and the part is not sold.

### Where they do not

**PCB row 3, layer count**

- *prior:* CANNOT DETERMINE - 'halo's 4 is measured; Apple's 4 is a guess nobody has confirmed'
- *now:* SAME. Apple's 4 is COUNTED from a published physical delayering, and the superposition reading that would have made those four files carry no count was falsified at a named spot.
- *why it changed:* the evidence arrived after that page was generated. The prior verdict was correct for its state of knowledge. THIS CLOSES ONE OF THE PRIOR PAGE'S THREE CANNOT DETERMINE PCB ROWS.

**PCB row 1, outer diameter**

- *prior:* SAME - '26.0000 mm on the major axis, inside Apple's stated ~26 mm'
- *now:* SAME, but on a different basis. Apple's '~26 mm' has since been retracted (E04 -> E05: four methods that could not disagree, because all four applied a scalar px/mm to an anisotropic projection). Apple's OD is now a BOUND 24.95-26.34 mm with a signed downward expectation. rev_a's 26.0000 is still inside it. THE VERDICT SURVIVES; THE REASON UNDER IT DOES NOT.

**components row 15, the 2.4 GHz antenna**

- *prior:* 'AE1 - a rim inverted-F... ce-rf models +0.521 dBi, 3.7 dB above Apple's published figure'
- *now:* CONTRADICTED BY rev_a's OWN FILE on both halves. Topology: board.py builds 'the meandered quarter-wave monopole' and the owner describes a nine-tooth meander. Performance: board.py's WHAT THIS BOARD DOES NOT CLAIM section says the element is a parametric placeholder, that lane T3's round-board cases resonate at 4.0 and 5.8 GHz instead of 2.44 on a different outline, and that 'Its S11 is CANNOT DETERMINE until ce-rf measures THIS copper. It is not asserted to work.'
- *why it matters:* IT IS THE ONE ROW WHERE THE PRIOR PAGE CLAIMS rev_a BEATS APPLE ON A PHYSICAL NUMBER, and rev_a's own source file withdraws it. Apple's -3.2 dBi is a measurement of a shipped antenna; +0.521 dBi is a model of a placeholder. Comparing them was never valid.
- *not fixed here:* halo_rev_a and spec/comparison.json belong to other live sessions. Read, not written. Routed to the orchestrator.

### What this file adds that the prior one could not

- A THIRD COLUMN. The prior page is Apple vs halo. Nothing had ever set our two boards against each other, which is the only way to ask whether a divergence was worth making.
- A NAMED JUDGING AXIS PER ROW. The prior page's verdicts (SAME/EQUIVALENT/DIVERGED) describe a relationship; they never say which object is better, so 'DIVERGED' reads as a demerit even on the five rows where the divergence is the right call.
- A DIVERGENCE COUNTER. THE-DRIFT.md asked for one and nothing had built it.
- THE UNSTARTED / CANNOT DETERMINE SPLIT. The prior page has no way to say 'nobody has tried yet', so the Replica's four unstarted axes would have been filed as limits rather than as the one job they actually are.

| **halo_replica** | NOT DRAWN. The SoC is one of the neutral-black packages M08 could not separate — the single most important part on the board, and the Replica has no footprint for it. | CANNOT DETERMINE | board/CLOSING.md section 4 and section 5 gap 2. |

*Against Apple:* **halo_rev_a DIVERGED** — nRF54L10 for nRF52832, on a stated and priced reason (D12). **halo_replica CANNOT DETERMINE** — the processor has no footprint on this board.

A replica that cannot place the processor has not replicated the board — and it says so, which is why this row can be written honestly instead of being quietly absent.

*Would settle it:* the boundary-based dark-package detector in CLOSING.md section 5 gap 2. The packages are UNMISTAKABLE TO THE EYE by their straight boundaries; the gap is a METHOD gap, not a source gap, and a 1.9x-resolution source has already been tested and does not close it by luma or texture.

> **On G: halo_rev_a.** the divergence is what delivers GOAL.md section 3. Channel Sounding is peer ranging; nRF52832 has none.

> **On power: Apple.** Apple senses at ~50 nA; rev_a's 4.7M/4.7M divider draws 319 nA — 6.4x more, continuously, from a cell whose whole budget this project argues about in microamps. Neither of our boards beats Apple on this number and the Replica does not have one.

> **On THE SIGNED EXPECTATION: n/a.** AND THIS IS THE PART THAT MUST NOT BE MISREAD. M02 sec.8 records that IF THE OD BOUND MOVES, IT MOVES DOWN. So the Replica's 19 copper-to-edge violations get WORSE, not better, as the outer diameter resolves toward the 24.95 mm floor. Classifying them BOUND-LIMITED records WHOSE PROBLEM THEY ARE. It must never be read as expecting them to go away - they cannot be waited out, and the expectation runs against us.

## How to reproduce

```bash
cd ce-designs/halo/electronics/halo_replica
python3 tools/k_threeway.py check -v      # every anchor, with its file and value
python3 tools/k_threeway.py selftest      # 9 deliberate breaks, each watched going red
python3 tools/k_threeway.py render        # regenerate this page
```

`check` exits 0 PASS / 1 FAIL / 2 CANNOT DETERMINE. It verifies that this page agrees with the files it cites; it cannot verify that those files are right, and says so in its own docstring.
